plain_english: Never say "I lost it." Say "I gave it back." Did your child die? You gave them back. Did your wife die? You gave her back. Did someone take your property? You gave that back too. "But the person who took it was evil." What does that matter to you? The one who gave it to you in the first place took it back through whatever hands he chose. While you're allowed to have these things, treat them like something that isn't really yours. Think of yourself as a traveler staying at an inn.
original_excerpt: Never say of anything, “I have lost it,” but, “I have restored it.” Has your child died? It is restored. Has your wife died? She is restored. Has your estate been taken away? That likewise is restored. “But it was a bad man who took it.” What is it to you by whose hands he who gave it has demanded it again? While he permits you to possess it, hold it as something not your own, as do travelers at an inn.
